exposure: maternal trace element exposure (cobalt, molybdenum, rubidium, zinc)
antibiotic usage shortly before or on the delivery day
mode of birth (vaginal delivery, c-section delivery)
outcome: composition and similarity of mother-infant gut microbiota
cohort: The study included mother-infant dyads from whom longitudinal microbiota data was examined.
finding: Maternal exposure to trace elements, including Co, Mo, Rb, and Zn, and antibiotic usage, significantly influences the composition, dynamics, and intergenerational similarity of gut microbiota in mother-infant dyads.
mod_finding: The intergenerational effect of rubidium on meconium Bifidobacterium abundance was strengthened in the vaginal delivery group without antibiotic usage but attenuated in the C-section delivery group.
